newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends marginally up after stg softens.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends marginally up after stg softens.

text.p: London cocoa futures inched up on Monday afternoon as sterling's softer tone helped the market wipe off earlier losses in an otherwise uneventful day. But of the 7,280-lot turnover, some 3,000 were marked as AAs on the spot December. There was also a spate of Dec/March switches which widened to 37 stg a tonne at the close. "It's a dead day," said one trader.
"It's all about Dec liquidation as Friday is the last trading day before expiry," said another.
The benchmark March position ended two stg up on the day at 927 stg a tonne, just off a high of 928 and after a morning low of 920. December shed three stg to 890 at the close.
Most other contracts registered minor gains but volume was insignificant.

Sterling was off its highs against the dollar and mark in late European dealings. But the UK budget on Tuesday may give it another another shot in the arm if Chancellor Kenneth Clarke announces a hike in interest rates.

New York's shallow performance just above chart support disappointed London players who had expected a more decisive action at least at the beginning of the week before the Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday and Friday.

Earlier they said the CFTC Commitment of Traders Report released on Friday was bullish as it showed a net total speculative short position of 2,782 lots by November 19 after an increase in shorts and a decrease in longs in the preceding two weeks.
Physical news was scarce, but Ivorian arrivals at the end of this month may throw some light to estimates on the size of the crop.
In the meantime, traders expect London to hover within its current range with resistance at 934-935 stg basis March and support at 917 and 914, followed by 903.
"940 is a sell at the moment but 910-900 is a buy," said one trader.
